plan.visual_reading: The arc opens on the killing thirst itself — the parched, cracked-lipped face of a crucified man gasping two words — then steps back to David at his lamp, glimpsing a death not his own, and lays out the psalm's three dying images: strength dried to a potsherd, the tongue cleaving to the jaws, the body sinking into the dust of death. The proof beat brings the cross John records and holds David and Calvary a thousand years apart in one dusk. The conviction turns on the central irony — the Maker of every river and sea hanging parched with nothing in His hands while, behind Him, all the waters He made dim into shadow; the well of John 4 and the offer of living water sit beside Him. Two OT water-echoes the NT names (the smitten rock that was Christ, 1 Cor 10:4; the open invitation 'every one that thirsteth, come', Isaiah 55:1 / 44:3) carry the landing toward a weary soul drinking and never thirsting again, and the cut lands on the hero: the crucified Christ with living water drawn from His own pierced side — that water is Himself.
plan.red_team_notes: Jaded Viewer worries: (1) too many crucified-Christ frames could blur — answered by varying framing hard (close parched face / mid cry / low-angle full body / wide pierced-side hero) and giving each a distinct macro payload. (2) The potsherd and the tongue-cleaving close-ups risk being grim medical shots — kept reverent and held-as-state, not gore. (3) The Ps 69 landmine: I deliberately do NOT depict the vinegar sponge (its fulfilment formula belongs to Ps 69:21) — the cross scenes show thirst, not the sponge, so no visual implies a Ps 22 citation. (4) The water-echo scenes could be a Sunday-school water montage — anchored each to a real NT-named echo (the Rock = Christ, 1 Cor 10:4; the thirst-invitation Isaiah 55:1/44:3 behind John 7:37) so they read as study, not slideshow. (5) Rejected the obvious cliche auto-completes: a literal glowing chalice, a dripping faucet, a desert mirage, a single falling teardrop standing for the whole psalm.

plan.rationale: Chose the three psalm images the verse actually names (potsherd / tongue / dust) over a single generic dying-body shot, so the 'point' beat reads as study not illustration. Kept the cross varied across four framings to avoid a blur of identical crucifixions. Anchored both OT-echo water scenes to real NT-named texts (the Rock = Christ, 1 Cor 10:4; the thirst-invitation Isaiah 55:1/44:3 behind John 7:37) rather than reaching for an un-cited type. Hero is the pierced-side living-water Christ (John 19:34) because 'that water is Himself' is the CTA — the cut must land there, not on the most harrowing thirst frame. Rejected the glowing chalice, the single teardrop, the desert mirage, and the vinegar sponge (the last on the Ps 69 guard).

panel.note: The arc drives the turn: hook #1 'Two Words on a Cross' states the thirst, the 'point' images (#3 potsherd / #4 tongue / #5 dust) ground the verse, #7 'A Thousand Years Apart' carries the proof, #8 'Who Made Every River' lands the conviction irony, and #14 'That Water Is Himself' closes the gospel. Not just illustration.

Watch #6 'The Cry Recorded' and #14 — both crucifixion scenes; the plan deliberately omits the vinegar sponge to keep clear of the Ps 69:21 fulfilment the spoken text never claims. Confirm the renderer keeps #14's side-stream as water-and-blood (John 19:34), not an invented fountain. OT echoes #11 (1 Cor 10:4) and #12 (Isaiah 55:1/44:3) are NT-anchored, not stretched.

#12 'Come, Every One That Thirsteth' risks generic 'people-at-a-spring' stock religious art; its specific vignettes (cracked ground drinking, new green shoots, empty vessels held out) and the Isaiah anchor pull it back from merchandise. The rest hold a sceptical scroller.

jesus_variant is consistent: passion on every crucifixion scene (#1, #6, #8, #10, #14), ministry on the John 4 well (#9), null on the OT/symbol scenes (#2-5, #11-13). Same thorn-crowned, spent passion Christ across the cross frames; the well Christ is the calm ministry figure.

14 scenes within the rich-passage window; subject_blocks are state-only ('lips parted around a word left unspoken', 'a bright sheet of water caught across its face') with no spooking action verbs; every scene earns its slot via a distinct macro payload.

Three psalm close-ups in a row (#3 potsherd, #4 tongue, #5 dust) could feel like a checklist; they are saved by being the literal objects the verse names and by hard framing variety. No cliche-blocklist auto-completes — the glowing chalice, single teardrop, and heaven-beam were explicitly rejected in candidates.

paper_cohesion.notes: The set coheres around one spine: the killing thirst of Psalm 22:15 (#1 hook, #3-5 the three named images) -> the cross where it was spoken (#6) held a thousand years from David (#7) -> the conviction irony that the Maker of every water thirsts with nothing in His hands (#8/#10) while He offers living water (#9) -> two NT-named OT water echoes (#11 the Rock = 1 Cor 10:4; #12 Isaiah 55:1/44:3 'come, every one that thirsteth') -> the thirst stilled (#13) -> the hero close where the living water is drawn from Christ's own pierced side (#14). The thread is mirrored at the centre (#8) and lands on the gospel-pivot, exactly as required. The descriptive-match guard holds across the set — no scene depicts the vinegar sponge, so nothing visually asserts the Psalm 69 fulfilment the narration deliberately avoids. jesus_variant is consistent set-wide. No palette or character conflict; the five crucifixion scenes are differentiated by framing and theological function rather than repeating. No structural failure.
